answer: A crystal workshop could make each earning key solve a fresh computational puzzle before admission. Validators derive its seed from an unpredictable beacon, the key and epoch, then verify the proof cheaply; copying a proof to a mirror account fails. Each alias must forge a separate proof, consuming additional computation and electricity even across a parallel farm. Set that cost above the extra per-key subsidy. This assumes an unbiased beacon and no cheap puzzle shortcut; newcomers can join with a small, published hardware budget.
